title: Evidence Does Not Remove the Infinite Quantifier
mathematical_role: Separate finite zero verification, partial critical-line theorems, heuristic or random-matrix evidence, and the universal Riemann hypothesis.
learning_objective: Distinguish bounded, partial, and heuristic evidence from the all-zeros quantifier of RH.
literal_semantics: Finite verification certifies only a bounded zero range.
Critical-line theorems establishing many zeros on Re(s)=1/2 remain partial rather than universal.
Random-matrix and spectral analogies are heuristic evidence, not proof.
RH quantifies over every nontrivial zero and remains open.
nonliteral_semantics: The plate reports no new zero-verification height or proportion.
No empirical or heuristic panel is promoted into theorem or proof authority.

notes: Candidate semantics are bounded by the existing documentary source; no new mathematical source is admitted by this visual operation.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG generator v1
reproducibility_notes: The generator uses no network, randomness, timestamps, or external data.
Repository tests compare generator output byte-for-byte with the committed SVG candidate.
Text uses ASCII mathematical notation where practical to reduce missing-glyph risk in supported render paths.

accessibility.alt_text: Four panels distinguish finite zero verification, partial critical-line results, heuristic evidence, and the universal Riemann hypothesis, which remains open.
accessibility.long_description: The first panel is finite verification, the second partial critical-line results, the third heuristics and random-matrix models, and the fourth the universal RH statement. The lower text explains that stronger bounded evidence does not automatically cross the logical gap to proof.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: The plate accurately classifies common RH evidence by logical scope and keeps the universal statement distinct.
not_claimed: A proof of the Riemann hypothesis

supersession_reason: Replace content-poor or metaphor-compressed predecessor with a literal, domain-bounded teaching representation.
